subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which tool-result visibility policy should OpenClaw use for the DeepSeek prefix-cache regression without breaking information-bearing tools?
rationale: Code inspection can show that broad placeholdering breaks normal tool-result semantics, but the acceptable permanent policy for heartbeat/status versus exec/read/search/memory outputs needs maintainer product ownership and live provider proof.

options.title: Require a narrow approved policy
options.body: Ask the contributor to remove broad zero-content summaries for information-bearing tools, port the fix to current `packages/ai` paths, and prove the selected heartbeat/status policy with live DeepSeek telemetry.

options.title: Accept broad suppression knowingly
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the risk that existing agents will no longer see normal tool outputs after calls to the listed tools.

options.title: Pause for a canonical cache strategy
options.body: Leave this PR paused or close it later only if another proof-positive provider-cache PR becomes the selected fix for the same user problem.

recommendation.title: Require a narrow approved policy
recommendation.body: Ask the contributor to remove broad zero-content summaries for information-bearing tools, port the fix to current `packages/ai` paths, and prove the selected heartbeat/status policy with live DeepSeek telemetry.
